references.text: The warning about bearing sin and dying as a consequence of profaning holy things, corresponding to the warning in Numbers 18:32 not to profane the holy offerings of the people of Israel.
Prohibition against profaning the holy offerings that the people of Israel present to the Lord, with a warning of guilt for eating them unworthily.
The context of the Levites' service and the warning that the people of Israel must not approach the tabernacle to avoid sin and death.
The command to lift up the best portion from the tithe, closely linked to verse 32 regarding not bearing sin when the best is given.
The fat (chelev), as the best part of the sacrifice, corresponding to the best portion that must be lifted from the tithe in Numbers 18:32.
The warning about bearing sin and dying through improper handling of holy things in the sanctuary.
Whoever profanes the Lord's holy things shall be cut off from their people, parallel to the warning of death in Numbers 18:32.
